leads.name: The Robertson Oak (Pitlochry)
leads.reason: One readable source (a 2026 blog visit, alive end of January and May 2026): sessile oak thought over 350 years, beside the gates of a sewage works south of Pitlochry, plaque by Clan Donnachaidh, Jacobite legend of George Robertson of Faskally hiding after Culloden (tradition, not documented). Another source says over 500 years and a different site (distillery grounds); no coordinate, no second source read. No photo or exact pin in reach.

leads.name: Dunkeld Pedestal Larch
leads.reason: Larch about 300 years old with a root 'pedestal' almost 8 m across, in woods behind Dunkeld House Hotel (hotel grounds, access to the woods not confirmed). The only locating source found was a blog that took its position from the Woodland Trust Ancient Tree Inventory (off limits) and that itself failed to find it for a long search. No pin, no access evidence.
leads.species_basis: genus read from the tree's own name; ask the reader which species

leads.name: Original Japanese Larches, Dunkeld House Hotel drive
leads.reason: Blog says planted 1887 by the 7th Duke near the main drive; Big Tree Country says 11 of the original 1785 Japanese larches stand on Kennel Bank. Dates conflict (1785 vs 1887), no pin, a group not a point.

leads.name: Cedar of Lebanon at Hermitage Bridge, The Hermitage
leads.reason: Wikipedia only: a Cedar of Lebanon beside the 1770 Hermitage Bridge, believed the oldest tree at the Hermitage. NTS ground, free path. Needs a second source and a pin; not searched further this pass.

leads.name: Cluny Redwood (Cluny House Gardens, near Aberfeldy)
leads.reason: Appears in the 2026 Heritage Trees of Scotland series (#6); not researched this pass. Candidate for a later Aberfeldy pass.

leads.name: Scone Palace Pinetum and giant sequoia
leads.reason: Palace pinetum of rare conifers collected by the 4th Earl of Mansfield; a giant sequoia is listed on monumentaltrees.com (fact lead only). No measurements or coordinates read this pass.

blocked.name: Hermitage Douglas-fir (Dunkeld)
blocked.reason: Dead: blown down in the early hours of 13 January 2017 (Wikipedia; Perth and Kinross Countryside Trust news 'Friday 13th proves unlucky for Britain's 3rd tallest tree'); a 2026 blog visit also found the book's tree gone.
